The 'Moral Majority' and Focus on the Family

source: original; stimulus photograph viewed before writing

stimulus.source_note: Photograph: Reverend Jerry Falwell at an 'I Love America' rally, Ohio Statehouse, Columbus, Ohio, September 17, 1979, by David E. Lucas (Columbus Metropolitan Library, via DPLA/Wikimedia Commons), public domain. Account drawn from the grounding books (Barron's Ch. 10, Topic 8.14; 5 Steps Ch. 28; Princeton Ch. 12).
stimulus.text: The photograph shows the Reverend Jerry Falwell speaking into a microphone on the steps of the Ohio Statehouse in Columbus, Ohio, on September 17, 1979, at an 'I Love America' rally. Behind him stands a choir of young men in white suits and young women in long red dresses with their heads bowed, and six American flags stand before the building's stone columns.

stem: The rallies best show which change in American religion and politics in the 1970s?

options.text: Evangelical Protestants left politics entirely during the 1970s and never returned to it.
options.misconception: The photograph shows evangelicals rallying on capitol steps in 1979, so they entered politics, not left it.

options.text: Catholics and evangelicals refused to work together on any political issue at all.
options.misconception: Background: After Roe v. Wade, evangelicals and Catholics joined in opposing abortion, the opposite of refusing to work together.

options.text: Religion disappeared completely from American public life right after Roe in 1973.
options.misconception: The photograph shows a public religious rally in 1979, so religion had not disappeared.

options.text: Evangelicals who had long stayed out of politics began organizing as a political force.

rationales.A: The photograph shows evangelicals rallying on capitol steps in 1979, so they entered politics, not left it.
rationales.B: Background: After Roe v. Wade, evangelicals and Catholics joined in opposing abortion, the opposite of refusing to work together.
rationales.C: The photograph shows a public religious rally in 1979, so religion had not disappeared.
rationales.D: Background: Evangelicals had long kept religion and politics apart, but Falwell's rallies broke that rule and turned believers into voters.
rationales.general:
1. The photograph is dated 1979 and shows a preacher leading a political rally on capitol steps.
2. Background: Evangelicals had long kept religion and politics apart, and Falwell broke that rule.
3. The rally is the change itself: believers who once stayed out of politics now organized as voters.
Remember: A photograph's date and place can show a change that words alone would only claim.
